issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff changes the RNG seed (12345 to 0), adds uniform random starting points (20% of tries), shifts the mix of the other start types and raises the search time limit from 150 to 200 s. There is no file access and no pasted coordinates. The solver still computes the radii (LP + polish).
No bug that would make the result meaningless. The validity check is unchanged and the candidate run gave a valid result (-2.6353).

Time risk: the loop now runs for 200 s. If the last try's LP/polish starts just before the cutoff, plus any final polish, the job can pass the ~4-minute (240 s) margin and get near the 5-minute kill. This hurts reliability but is not grounds for a veto.
The loop stops on the wall clock, so results depend on machine speed even with a fixed seed. The incumbent already does this.

The numbers support the provisional reject. The candidate loss (-2.6353) is 0.0007 higher, so worse, than the incumbent (-2.6360). Both values are below the reference 2.635 radii sum, so neither beats the best known result.

z cannot be checked properly: the incumbent has 1 run and the candidate has 1 run, so there is no variance estimate. The reported |z| of about 463 only works out if the noise is assumed to be about 1.5e-6 (roughly sqrt(2) times the 1e-6 run-to-run noise). The reject decision does not depend on z, because the candidate is worse in every case.
